text: Layers generally scavenge but will sit (brood) for a full day once a clutch is laid. Housing layers offers a quiet, shady place to lay undisturbed by cocks; appropriate nests (a basket- or pot-like space with a 25 cm base diameter, 18 cm high walls, and a 40 cm open top diameter); water and feed available in the shelter to limit weight loss during brooding; and protection of both layers and eggs from predators.
